schemes.name: Help to Buy (HTB) Scheme
schemes.description: The Help to Buy incentive is a scheme for first-time buyers of newly built homes. It allows you to claim a refund of income tax and DIRT paid over the previous 4 tax years, up to €30,000.
eligibility: First-time buyer only
Property must be a newly built home or self-build
Property value must not exceed €500,000
Mortgage must be at least 70% of the property value
You must live in the property as your main home for 5 years
benefits: Applies to income tax and DIRT paid in last 4 years
Can be used towards your deposit
Available for both new builds and self-builds
schemes.how_to_apply: Apply through Revenue's myAccount or ROS. You must apply online before the property is purchased. Your contractor or solicitor also needs to be registered with Revenue.

schemes.name: First Home Scheme
schemes.description: The First Home Scheme is a shared equity scheme where the government and participating lenders pay up to 30% of the cost of a new home on your behalf. You own 100% of the property but the state holds an equity share.
eligibility: Must be a first-time buyer
New build properties only
Must have mortgage approval from a participating lender
Property price limits vary by county
Income limits apply
benefits: No repayments on equity share for first 5 years
schemes.how_to_apply: Apply at firsthomescheme.ie after receiving mortgage approval from a participating bank. The scheme is administered by the Housing Agency.

schemes.name: Local Authority Home Loan
schemes.description: A government-backed mortgage for first-time buyers and Fresh Start applicants who cannot get sufficient financing from commercial lenders. Offers competitive fixed interest rates.
eligibility: First-time buyer or Fresh Start applicant
Insufficient mortgage offer from two lenders
Minimum age 18
Income limits: single €70,000, joint €85,000 (higher in some counties)
Minimum income €15,000 (net)
benefits: Borrow up to 90% of property value
Available for new and second-hand properties
schemes.how_to_apply: Apply online at localauthorityhomeloan.ie or through your local authority housing office. You will need proof of income, ID, and bank statements.

schemes.name: Local Authority Affordable Purchase
schemes.description: Local authorities provide new homes at reduced prices to eligible buyers. The local authority retains an equity stake proportional to the discount given, which can be bought out over time.
eligibility: First-time buyer or Fresh Start applicant
Must be unable to afford a home at market price
Income limits apply by county
Must be able to service the mortgage
benefits: Homes sold at below market price
Local authority equity share can be redeemed over time
schemes.how_to_apply: Register interest with your local authority. When affordable schemes open, eligible applicants are selected. Check your local authority website for available schemes.

schemes.name: Housing Assistance Payment (HAP)
schemes.description: HAP is a social housing support for people with a long-term housing need. Your local authority pays your rent directly to your private landlord and you pay a weekly HAP contribution based on your income.
eligibility: Must be on or qualify for the social housing list
Income limits apply
Property must meet HAP standards
Landlord must agree to participate
Available in your local authority area
benefits: Freedom to choose your own rental accommodation
Can take up full-time employment and stay on HAP
schemes.how_to_apply: Apply to your local authority housing department. You will need to be assessed for social housing and find a landlord willing to accept HAP.

schemes.name: Rent Supplement
schemes.description: Rent Supplement is a short-term means-tested income support payment to help with the cost of private rented accommodation for people who cannot provide for their own housing needs.
eligibility: Must meet income limits
Must have been renting for at least 6 months (183 days) of the last 12 months, or have immediate housing need
Rent must be within Rent Supplement limits
Must be habitually resident in Ireland
Not in full-time employment (30+ hours/week)
benefits: Weekly payment to help cover rent
Can be paid to you or directly to landlord
schemes.how_to_apply: Apply at your local Intreo Centre, Social Welfare Branch Office, or online at MyWelfare.ie.

schemes.name: Cost Rental / Affordable Rental
schemes.description: Cost Rental provides long-term affordable rented homes for middle-income households who earn too much for social housing but cannot afford private market rents. Rents are set at cost, not profit.
eligibility: Net household income €53,000–€120,000 (Dublin, varies by area)
Must not own a property
Must be able to afford the cost rental price
Priority for those on housing lists
benefits: Long-term security of tenure (tenancy of indefinite duration)
Managed by AHBs with professional standards
schemes.how_to_apply: Properties advertised through Housing Agency, Approved Housing Bodies, and local authority websites. Register interest when schemes open.

schemes.name: Social Housing (Local Authority)
schemes.description: Local authority housing is provided to people on low incomes who need long-term social housing. Rent is based on your income, usually a percentage of your household earnings.
eligibility: Must meet income limits for your area
Must have a housing need (cannot afford private rent)
Must be habitually resident in Ireland
Other qualifying criteria per local authority
schemes.how_to_apply: Apply to your local authority housing department. You will be assessed and placed on the social housing list. Allocation depends on need and availability.

schemes.name: Mortgage to Rent Scheme
schemes.description: If you are in serious mortgage arrears and at risk of losing your home, this scheme allows you to sell your home to an Approved Housing Body and remain living in it as a social housing tenant.
eligibility: Mortgage in arrears and unsustainable
Property is your principal private residence
Qualify for social housing
Property value within scheme limits
Lender agrees to participate
benefits: Stay in your home as a social housing tenant
schemes.how_to_apply: Contact your mortgage lender, MABS (mabs.ie), or Abhaile service. Your lender or financial advisor can initiate the process with you.

schemes.name: Croí Cónaithe (Cities) Scheme
schemes.description: A government subsidy scheme that bridges the gap between the cost of building apartments and their market sale price, making newly built city apartments more affordable for owner-occupiers to purchase.
eligibility: Must be an owner-occupier (not investor)
Apartments in Dublin, Cork, Galway, Limerick, Waterford
New build apartments only
Clawback applies if sold within 10 years
Check Housing Agency for current availability
benefits: Reduces purchase price of new apartments
Makes city centre living more affordable
No repayment if you stay for 10+ years
schemes.how_to_apply: Apartments are advertised directly by developers participating in the scheme. Check the Housing Agency at housingagency.ie/CroiConaitheCities for current available developments.

schemes.name: Vacant Property Refurbishment Grant
schemes.description: A grant of up to €50,000 to renovate a vacant property anywhere in Ireland — cities, towns or rural areas — to use as your home or as a rental. Up to €70,000 if the property is derelict. Funded through the Croí Cónaithe Towns Fund.
eligibility: Property must have been vacant for 2+ years
Must be built up to and including 2007
Must own the property or be actively purchasing it
Property must become your principal private residence or a rental
Cannot start works before grant approval
benefits: Applies nationwide — cities, towns, villages and rural
Can also be used for rental properties
schemes.how_to_apply: Apply through your local authority housing section before starting any works. Download the application form at gov.ie/en/service/f8f1b-vacant-property-refurbishment-grant/

schemes.name: SEAI Home Energy Upgrade Grants
schemes.description: SEAI offers grants to homeowners and landlords for energy efficiency improvements including insulation, heat pumps, solar panels and windows.
eligibility: Own your home (homeowners and landlords)
Home built before 2011 for most measures
Work must be done by SEAI registered contractors
Apply before starting work
benefits: Multiple measures covered in one application
Reduces energy bills and carbon footprint
schemes.how_to_apply: Apply at seai.ie/grants before starting any work. Choose an SEAI registered contractor. Grants are paid directly to your contractor reducing upfront costs.

schemes.name: Warmer Homes Scheme (Free Upgrades)
schemes.description: A fully funded scheme providing FREE energy efficiency upgrades for homeowners who receive qualifying social welfare payments. Includes insulation, heating upgrades, and more at no cost.
eligibility: Must own your home
Receive Fuel Allowance, Job Seeker's Allowance, or other qualifying payments
Home built before 2006
Live in the home as main residence
benefits: Completely free upgrades — no cost to homeowner
schemes.how_to_apply: Apply online at seai.ie/grants/fully-funded-upgrades or call the Warmer Homes helpline at 1800 250 204.

schemes.name: Housing Adaptation Grant for Disability
schemes.description: A local authority grant to help adapt a home for a person with a physical, sensory or intellectual disability or serious illness. Updated December 2024 — maximum grant now €40,000.
eligibility: Person with disability living in the home
Medically necessary adaptations required
Income means test applies
Private homeowner or tenant (with landlord consent)
Tax affairs must be in order
benefits: Covers stairlifts, ramps, wet rooms, widened doorways
Improves independence and quality of life
schemes.how_to_apply: Apply through your local authority housing section. You will typically need a report from an Occupational Therapist. Your GP or public health nurse can refer you.

schemes.name: Mobility Aids Housing Grant
schemes.description: A grant for people with mobility difficulties to fund minor adaptations to the home such as grab rails, access ramps, level access showers or stairlifts. Updated December 2024 — maximum grant now €8,000.
eligibility: Mobility difficulties affecting daily living
Gross household income under €37,500 (updated Dec 2024)
Works must be medically recommended
Private homeowner or long-term tenant
benefits: Improves safety and independence at home
Same form used for all 3 housing adaptation grants
schemes.how_to_apply: Apply through your local authority housing section with a medical recommendation. Download the application form at gov.ie or from your local authority.
